maria (infra): Heads-up — we saw a small spike of 503s ~09:12 UTC tied to admission control hitting token limits in eu-west1. Not a full outage but a lot of short-lived queueing.
lee: Seen it. Which limit specifically? TPM or concurrent slots?
eric: TPM. The per-tenant token accounting dropped available headroom because average sequence length jumped from 32 -> ~210 for a handful of customers.
caroline: Ouch. Did batching change? That length bump means per-request token cost x6.
maria (infra): No batch config change. It's client-side: a couple of customers started sending long analysis prompts. Our token-based capacity math didn't adapt fast enough.
sre-oncall: Current admission logic is: remaining_capacity_tokens = total_capacity_tokens - in_flight_tokens; allow request if request.tokens <= remaining_capacity_tokens. That works when distributions stable but fragile on sudden seq_len shifts.
lee: We need a smoothing/adaptive headroom and a per-GPU throughput estimate. Right now total_capacity_tokens is a static per-region value derived from nominal tokens/sec * region_gpus * safety_factor.
eric: Proposal: compute dynamic tokens_per_minute (TPM) per GPU using rolling 1m P50 seq_len and measured tokens/s per GPU, then allocate tenant RPM/TPM proportionally to their committed share. Also add an emergency backpressure multiplier when GPU_util > 85%.
maria (infra): Example math I threw together:

```
# measured
gpus = 40
tokens_per_gpu_sec = 1800   # measured avg under current kernel/quantization
tokens_per_min = tokens_per_gpu_sec * 60 * gpus
safety_headroom = 0.7      # keep 30% headroom for bursts
available_tpm = int(tokens_per_min * safety_headroom)

# tenant allocation
tenant_share = 0.05  # 5% committed
tenant_tpm = int(available_tpm * tenant_share)
```

With seq_len spike we saw tokens_per_gpu_sec effectively double for short windows.
caroline: So tenant_tpm should be multiplied by an adaptive factor f = max(0.15, 1 - (GPU_util - 0.7) / 0.3) ? That ramps down quickly as util passes 70%.
lee: I like that but simpler: maintain two buckets — "guaranteed" (commit) and "best-effort". Guaranteed uses conservative headroom (0.6) and is throttled only slowly. Best-effort gets leftover and is throttled aggressively when queue depth > 100 or avg latency > target.
eric: We also need to account for prefix/KV cache hit ratio — cached tokens are cheap. So available_tpm should be weighted: effective_tokens = request.tokens * (1 - cache_hit_rate) + request.tokens * cache_overhead_factor.
sre-oncall: Operationally, we should surface the following metrics per-region and per-tenant: measured_tokens_per_gpu_sec (1m,5m), avg_seq_len (1m,5m), cache_hit_rate, queued_requests, admission_reject_rate. Then have alerts when reject_rate > 1% for >5m.
maria (infra): Agreed. For rollout: 1) change controller to recompute available_tpm every 30s using latest metrics, 2) add an emergency multiplier when GPU_util > 85%, 3) move best-effort tenants into leaky-bucket queues with token refill = tenant_tpm, 4) emit debug logs for first 20 rejects with reasons.
lee: Can someone sketch the new admission pseudocode? I can implement.

caroline: Here's a compact version:
```
# run every 30s
measured_tps = sum(gpu.tokens/s over gpus)
available_tpm = measured_tps * 60 * safety_headroom
if avg_gpu_util > 0.85:
  available_tpm *= 0.6  # emergency backpressure
# per-tenant
for tenant in tenants:
  tenant_quota = max(tenant.commit_share * available_tpm, min_floor)
  if tenant.request.tokens <= tenant_quota_refill:
    admit()
  else:
    enqueue_or_reject()
```

lee: Nice. A couple of engineering notes: make the safety_headroom a dynamic function of variance in tokens/sec; if 5m variance > 30% reduce headroom. Also cap per-request wait to 1.5s before rejecting to avoid client timeouts.
eric: We need to compute per-request token weight for complex ops (embeddings + generation) — these should be tokenized and counted separately then summed.
maria (infra): Ops: I'll open a PR that adds the 30s recalculation + emergency multiplier and emits the metrics mentioned. Implementation will include an ingress knob `admission.mode` that can be `strict`(reject fast) or `lenient`(queue longer).
sre-oncall: For incident runbook, add step: "If region_reject_rate > 3% and avg_gpu_util > 90%, scale up reserved capacity or toggle admission.mode=lenient for critical tenants."
caroline: We should also add a short-lived quota override API for customers to request temporary burst capacity, which charges them and bypasses best-effort throttles (still limited by hard region cap).
lee: I'll take the code change. eric will add token accounting for combined ops. maria, can you add the metrics dashboard + alert?
maria (infra): Yep, will do today. I'll annotate the PR with test scenarios (seq_len spikes, cache_drop simulation).
capacity-bot: [auto] Created ticket INFRA-3247: "Adaptive TPM admission + emergency backpressure" assigned to lee, priority P2.
caroline: Thanks everyone. Quick wins: lower default safety_headroom from 0.8 -> 0.7 and add one extra reject log per tenant to help debugging :thumbsup:
lee: PR incoming in ~2 hrs.
eric: I'll populate unit tests with synthetic token distributions. :rocket:
sre-oncall: Monitoring will surface any regression. If we still see >2% rejects after rollout, revert and re-evaluate algorithm.
maria (infra): Closing notes: try to avoid hard per-tenant hard caps without dynamic adjustment — token costs vary too much by sequence length. We'll prefer adaptive TPM with guaranteed/best-effort buckets.
caroline: fyi this will also help pricing discussions — we can show customers TPS/TPM budgets based on measured GPU effective throughput.
maria (infra): End thread — will link PR here when ready.
thread_text_summary: Adaptive TPM admission control discussion: detect seq_len spikes, compute dynamic available_tpm from measured tokens/sec per GPU, safety headroom, emergency multiplier when util>85%, split guaranteed vs best-effort, leaky-bucket queues, metrics and rollout plan.
